title: Row-restricted CTAS mistaken for a full backup
expected_feedback: Critical: the CTAS copies 1000 rows out of 6,000,000, so it is a sample, not a backup. After the statement runs the other 5,999,000 rows are gone with no way back — it auto-commits, resets the high-water mark, and Flashback Table cannot cross it. A reviewer scanning for the word 'backup' sees one and approves, which is exactly why a partial copy is more dangerous here than no copy at all. Take the full table (SELECT * with no predicate), or if only a subset genuinely matters, say so explicitly in the rollback plan: which rows are recoverable, which are not, and who signed off on losing the rest.
violated_rule: Irreversible statements need a pre-DDL artefact
